audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart showed Renekton winning 'First item' and '2+ items' in both layers, while the packet levelChart and the page's own whys[5]/whys[6] prose both say Aatrox takes over once items land.
audit.why: packet.levelChart = [Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Skill, Aatrox, Aatrox]; whys[5] and whys[6] already describe Aatrox winning extended fights after his first item. The chart layers contradicted the prose.
audit.corrected: phases[5].side/win[5] and phases[6].side/win[6] flipped to Aatrox as a matched atomic group, ratings dropped to 4/10, and both whys rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text and whys[4] claimed World Ender 'extends his Q range' / 'extends his Q knockups'.
audit.why: Riot's own description of World Ender is: fears nearby minions, bonus attack damage, increased healing, bonus Move Speed, extended on takedown. No range or knockup modification. Riot text is the authority over remembered older behaviour.
audit.corrected: Both now state bonus AD, Move Speed and increased healing on a 120/100/80s cooldown, and key the commit to R being down. 'mid' had the same claim and was corrected in place.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Deathbringer Stance auto-reset tell was absent, and dontsFull[1].d did not match its own title.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags 'autoreset-burst-tell': Aatrox's burst opens with a passive auto-attack reset, so the wind-up, not the ability cast, is the disengage cue. The kit confirms the autoReset flag on his passive.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now reads 'Deathbringer resets his auto — step out on the wind-up, not the cast.' Anti-heal (missingInteractions 'needs-antiheal') was already covered by the Executioner's Calling line in report[8], so nothing was duplicated.

audit.why: World Ender at 120/100/80s is correctly identified as the punishable cooldown throughout.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged "World Ender's" in spikes[1].text as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: False positive — the edit distance of 2 is the possessive apostrophe-s. World Ender is the real R name.

edits.before: Eclipse is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on World Ender's cooldown.
edits.after: His first item lands first: World Ender healing outlasts your burst — fight only while R is down.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Aatrox carry threat 8/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items of drain-heal beats your one rotation in side lane. Aatrox carry threat 8/10 — rotate and stun his carry instead.

edits.before: Both ults arrive simultaneously — Dominus gives you a 300+ HP buffer and back-to-back empowered Ws, but World Ender doubles his healing and extends his Q knockups, making this a genuine 50-50 all-in.
edits.after: Both ults arrive together — Dominus gives you a 300+ HP buffer and back-to-back empowered Ws, but World Ender adds AD, Move Speed and increased healing on a 120s timer, so commit only once it is down.

edits.before: Both ultimates arrive simultaneously and both change the math: Dominus gives you 300+ HP and back-to-back empowered Ws, but World Ender doubles his drain-heal and extends his Q range, making full all-ins a genuine coin flip.
edits.after: Both ultimates arrive at once: Dominus gives you 300+ HP and back-to-back empowered Ws, but World Ender's bonus AD, Move Speed and increased healing beat your rotation — all-ins are a coin flip unless his 120s R is down.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are your strongest relative window — he scales into World Ender but it has a long cooldown, and your empowered E armor-shred stacks with any Serrated Dirk you may have. Trade hard on its cooldown, respect the yellow sheen of World Ender activating and disengage immediately when you see it. At level 6 the matchup flattens: Dominus gives you back-to-back empowered Ws and a health buffer, but World Ender's healing and extended Q range mean a full commit can go either way — do not blow R trying to kill him under his tower where his Q sweetspots are easier to land.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are your strongest relative window — World Ender is a 120-second cooldown at rank 1, and your empowered E armor-shred stacks with any Serrated Dirk you may have. Trade hard on its cooldown, respect the yellow sheen of World Ender activating and disengage immediately when you see it. At level 6 the matchup flattens: Dominus gives you back-to-back empowered Ws and a health buffer, but World Ender's bonus AD and increased healing mean a full commit can go either way — do not blow R trying to kill him under his tower where his Q sweetspots are easier to land.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Deathbringer resets his auto — step out on the wind-up, not the cast.

notes: Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived 'grounding' flag that Riot's description does not support (drag to centre + damage only) — the mirror audit reached the same conclusion, so no grounding claim was made from either side. Renekton's Cull the Meek (Q) heals him and heals more above 50 Fury; Aatrox anti-heal is already in report[8], but the reverse (his Executioner's/Bramble on you) is not mentioned anywhere and there was no space to add it. Packet defect 'World Ender's' is a possessive false positive.
